units.content: Describes CGET tool suite as experimental instrumentation intended to evaluate hypothesized structural transformations, not directly measure intelligence.
Proposes measurement of compression, causal fidelity, execution efficiency, closure, steering bandwidth and identity preservation.
Each experiment should identify baseline, structural intervention, representation change, metric evaluation, capability change and failure analysis.
Manual derivatives->AD, assembly->compilers, minimax->alpha-beta and external cognitive interfaces are listed with expected CGET signatures.
Measurement implementation, historical case studies, synthetic agents and open research are future phases.
Experimental research program intended to make CGET measurable/falsifiable; no claim that the listed expected signatures are measured results.
Specifies CGET Analyzer as primary experimental instrument concept for decomposing transformations into compression, causal, execution, composition, agency and identity effects.
Proposed pipeline defines baseline S0, intervention S0->S1, structural differences and a CGET structural report rather than one intelligence score.
Defines intended analyzer modules/metrics for compression, causal fidelity, execution leverage, closure, steering bandwidth and identity stability.
YAML-like structural report is an example output schema with empty metric fields/classification, not a produced report.
Automatic-differentiation example qualitatively labels compression/fidelity/execution/composition/agency/identity effects; it is illustrative analysis, not instrument-generated measurement.
Strong CGET signature is proposed when complexity falls, causal fidelity/closure/control rise and identity loss approaches zero.
Source explicitly calls CGET Analyzer a conceptual prototype specification; automated implementation, synthetic environments, simulations and stress tests are future work.
Designs modular analyzer architecture over coupled state S=(G,O,T) and transformations S_t->S_t+1.
Proposes WorldModel, ObserverModel, Transformation and PolicyModel data structures corresponding to CGET formal objects.
Proposes compression, causal, execution, composition, agency and identity engines with example interfaces.
Input transformation -> represent S0/S1 -> measure structural differences -> constraints -> report.
Self-modification simulator, causal discovery, alignment stress tester and interface analysis are future extension points.
Architecture/design specification; example Python interfaces do not establish implemented modules or measured outputs.
Frozen blob is ordinary Python source without surrounding Markdown fences and is syntactically structured as importable toy metric functions.
Docstring calls functions toy implementations of CGET compression, causal fidelity, closure, agency, identity and transition metrics.
Implements compression_score, causal_fidelity, closure_score, agency_bandwidth, identity_preservation, transition_stability and theta_star as arithmetic functions.
Functions operationalize theoretical quantities using simple ratios/scalar changes; implementation choices are not validated equivalences to the formal CGET constructs.
Component code is executable in principle with standard Python/math, but no frozen execution record demonstrates use or empirical validity.
Implemented proxy function != validated metric != observed measurement.
Frozen blob is ordinary Python and imports local cget_metrics/toy_agents modules.
evaluate(agent) computes compression, causal, closure, agency, identity and theta from agent fields; run() constructs three toy agents and prints evaluation dictionaries.
All evaluation inputs come from hard-coded fields of toy_agents.py rather than environmental observations or logged interventions.
Direct run would print calculated synthetic agent dictionaries; no frozen run output is stored.
Executable synthetic calculator over programmed toy inputs; not an empirical experiment or instrument validation.
Documents structural metrics intended to decompose intelligence-like capability without a single scalar ranking.
Defines DeltaK, I_causal, L_compute, C(Omega), C_O, A_control, identity/core-loss and S_T metrics.
Source proposes hard causal/closure/identity/stability constraints before maximizing execution leverage times agency.
A strong intelligence signature is proposed when compression, causal fidelity, closure and control increase while core loss tends to zero.
Metric specification/interpretation; no validation that these formulas measure the intended latent properties is reported.
Frozen .py blob is literally wrapped in Markdown code fences and is not directly executable Python as stored.
Embedded code describes a complete toy benchmark over compression, fidelity, closure, agency, identity and Theta*.
Would import evaluate and hard-coded toy agents, print metrics, then rank Lookup/Causal/SelfModifying agents.

Ranks agents by Theta* despite documentation stating analyzer does not attempt a single intelligence score and benchmark design prefers lexicographic constraints; comment says future versions may replace scalar ranking.
Implementation/specification tension preserved: anti-scalar documentation vs scalar Theta* ranking code. No reconciliation authority.
Intended code prints per-agent metrics and a CGET transformation ranking; no execution record exists.
Fenced intended runner over synthetic toy inputs; not an executed benchmark.
Frozen blob is ordinary Python defining minimal toy agent data objects.
Defines Agent base plus LookupAgent, CausalAgent and SelfModifyingAgent/CGET Agent with fields consumed by analyzer metrics.
Complexity, intervention counts, composition counts, reachable/steerable counts and identity changes are manually assigned constants, not measured observations.
Programmed values encode an intended ordering from Lookup to Causal to SelfModifying/CGET agent; this is construction, not independent confirmation of the theory.
Executable synthetic fixtures, not empirical agents or data-generating experiments.
Explicitly describes CGET Benchmark Suite as a proposed evaluation framework for structural capability growth.
Proposes RCS, CFS, OCS, EES, CSB, AKS, CIPS, ALS and TSS with representation, intervention, composition, agency and self-modification tasks.
Benchmark avoids simple scalar optimization and proposes identity/causal/closure constraints before agency/efficiency optimization.
Rock/thermostat/ML/modern-agent/CGET-target table is example benchmark progression, not observed test output.
Lists representation, closure, agency, invariant-preservation and alignment conditions whose failure would challenge CGET predictions.
Proposed benchmark specification, not a completed benchmark or validation.
Source calls itself CGET Experimental Test Results and says it records evaluations of transformations through CGET structural metrics.
Status table labels automatic differentiation, compilers, alpha-beta and brute-force->learned-heuristic cases 'Initial Analysis'; raw->latent and static->self-modifying cases are 'Proposed'.

Qualitative retrospective analysis assigns positive compression, causal fidelity, execution gain, closure, agency and near-zero identity loss to automatic differentiation, classifying it Strong Intelligence-Enhancing Transformation.
Qualitative retrospective analysis assigns positive CGET structural effects to compiler abstraction and labels it Strong Positive Transformation.
Qualitative retrospective analysis assigns compression/fidelity/execution/closure/agency benefits and zero identity loss to alpha-beta pruning, labeling it Pure Computational Leverage Increase.
Brute-force->learned representation section states hypothesis, expected signature and failure condition rather than measured outcome.
Static optimizer->self-modifying agent section specifies identity, stability and agency tests plus expected success/failure signatures; source status remains proposed.

Source says initial qualitative experiments show a consistent pattern for AD, compilers and alpha-beta; learned representations are expected and self-modification remains unknown/central open problem.

No run metadata, raw measurements, seeds, logs, analyzer output or execution provenance accompanies the qualitative classifications; therefore SOURCE_LABELED_RESULT/FINDING != MEASURED_EXECUTION_RESULT.

branches: Analyzer/benchmark documentation rejects or de-emphasizes a single scalar intelligence score and prescribes lexicographic constraints
run_benchmark.py ranks toy agents by Theta*
